newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Broker barred from two Pakistani stock exchanges.
newsitem.headline: Broker barred from two Pakistani stock exchanges.

text.p: Pakistan's Corporate Law Authority (CLA) has barred stock broker Zafar Moti from the Karachi and Lahore stock exchanges on charges of violating trading laws, a CLA official said on Wednesday.
"The membership of Zafar Moti has been removed from both the exchanges with immediate effect for violating trading laws," a CLA spokesman said.
A CLA statement said Moti had defrauded Agha Arshad by failing to deliver listed shares for which Arshad had paid more than nine million rupees between February 1 and May 3, 1995.
Moti also sold shares worth more than one million rupees on behalf of the same client, but failed to pay him the proceeds.
The CLA said Moti had failed to disprove the client's complaints and had not produced any documents in his defence.
Moti was not immediately available for comment, but his father Siddiq Moti said an appeal against the CLA decision would be lodged with the authority's chairman.
"Right now I don't want to make any comment. I'll have to first consult my lawyer," he said.
A CLA official said Moti could appeal to the CLA chairman within 60 days or go to court.
"Zafar Moti took money from me about two years back but did not gave me any shares against it," Arshad told Reuters.
"I had also approached Karachi Stock Exchange officials with my complaint and a committee was formed, but it failed to resolve the issue, so I filed a petition with the CLA," he said.
The CLA issued a notice to the Lahore and Karachi stock exchanges on Wednesday ordering them not to let Moti trade.
The CLA official said it was the first time the authority had barred a stock exchange member for violating trading laws.
Dealers at the Karachi exchange said the CLA decision had dampened sentiment.

"Investors will be cautious for the time being...it will give a bad impression of the market," a dealer at a foreign brokerage house said. "But it should be taken as positive because it shows that there is a body which can intervene and protect the rights of investors."
Dealer Dawar Hasan said many investors were demoralised after the CLA action, which followed the banning of another broker from the Karachi bourse earlier this month.
"There is lot of uncertainty among investors because earlier the membership of M. Rashid Jamal's MRJ Securities was suspended for default by the Karachi exchange," Hasan said.
